comment: Play modes: where you watch (screen) and what you hold (controller). Setting names checked in RetroArch's source (configuration.c, v1.19.1): run_ahead_enabled, run_ahead_frames, run_ahead_hide_warnings, video_frame_delay_auto. Only cores that can run ahead cheaply on these handhelds get run-ahead.

screens.label: Handheld
screens.desc: Playing on the handheld's own screen.

screens.label: TV by cable
screens.desc: USB-C to HDMI cable or a dock.

screens.label: TV streamed
screens.desc: Screen mirroring, casting or a wireless display.

controllers.label: Wired controller
controllers.desc: A controller on a USB cable.

heavy_note: Run-ahead isn't used for {emulator}: it runs the game twice per frame, which is too heavy for this console and would cause slowdown.

tv-cable: On the TV, choose Game mode (or PC mode) for this input. TVs add their own delay for picture processing, and Game mode switches most of it off.
tv-stream: Streaming the picture to a TV adds delay that no setting on the handheld can remove. For action games, a USB-C to HDMI cable is much quicker.
On the TV, choose Game mode (or PC mode) for this input.
bluetooth: Keep the controller close to the handheld with nothing in between; Bluetooth gets slower when the signal is weak.
